title: Ankh
summary: Provides the Bun-first root command-line front door for discovering, planning, and dispatching independently released Ankh runtime providers.
purpose: Give users one stable CLI entrypoint while keeping domain behavior and provider ownership in standalone packages.
responsibilities: Discover compatible provider packages from the installed environment and current project.
Parse root commands, render provider-aware help, and dispatch commands to resolved provider handlers.
Expose inspectable provider command plans without taking ownership of domain execution.
boundaries: Does not implement the domain behavior owned by provider packages.
Does not hard-code provider categories or silently select unpublished provider source.
Does not compose application workflows or deployment infrastructure.
audience: Developers and operators invoking Ankhorage package capabilities from a terminal.
Provider package authors exposing commands through the Ankh runtime contract.
useCases: List available provider commands and render provider-specific help.
Dispatch a command to the exact compatible installed provider.
Inspect a provider command plan without executing the provider handler.

architecture.role: Thin CLI router and provider-discovery boundary over published Ankh runtime providers.
invariants: Domain behavior remains in independently released provider packages.
Provider resolution uses installed package identity and compatibility evidence.
Help, planning, and execution share the same provider discovery path.

limitations: Only installed and compatible providers with valid package metadata can be discovered.
